### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9476092c7ee64915749c2146a9ecbe5e139a7126` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9440da95de44b93cbc1fa4ebd1b2fda27cbee22e` — the merge of head `3551f0736f8e2485e2bc6b3ac45f780d189a5380` into base `9476092c7ee64915749c2146a9ecbe5e139a7126`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9440da95de44b93cbc1fa4ebd1b2fda27cbee22e && git checkout 9440da95de44b93cbc1fa4ebd1b2fda27cbee22e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9476092c7ee64915749c2146a9ecbe5e139a7126 3551f0736f8e2485e2bc6b3ac45f780d189a5380 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9476092c7ee64915749c2146a9ecbe5e139a7126 && git merge --no-ff 3551f0736f8e2485e2bc6b3ac45f780d189a5380

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9476092c7ee64915749c2146a9ecbe5e139a7126
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3551f0736f8e2485e2bc6b3ac45f780d189a5380`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37432 body and all 6 comments (claim 7202779669, amendment 7203965629, scope note 7182743879, os-dev-report 7203921910), the PR #37699 body and its 7-file list, `git diff origin/main...pr-37699-a`, and the check-runs on the head, latest attempts and the superseded ones.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff makes these accept-set and public-surface changes:

1. **New export `AI_CONTEXT_FIELD_UNPROVISIONED`** from `@objectstack/lint`'s main entry (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, +1 line). This is an additive public export. **Right.**
2. **New rule id `ai-context-field-unprovisioned`**, emitted by `validateAiContext`. It is registered at the `advisory` tier (`authoring-rules.ts`, "the save is never refused for them"), and `AiContextSeverity` is the type `'warning'` alone, so the rule cannot emit an error. No app that builds today stops building. **Right.**
   - Judged sites: the root's `fields`, each related list's `fields` (both through `unknownFields`), `body.field`, `where`, `orderBy`, and the link field, named or implied. Each site first requires the name to resolve in the merged field map, then requires it to be in `unprovisionedOf(object)`.
   - On a non-external object that set is empty, so the sites stay silent. An author-declared column is excluded by the spec. `sys_*` objects are never judged. The link is judged only when it resolves (a named reference to the root, or exactly one implied reference). Malformed links stay `ai-context-related-link-unknown`, and a missing name stays `ai-context-field-unknown`. No site warns on a name that has storage. The one edge case is inherited from the shared predicate; see N2.
   - Faithful reuse: `unprovisionedInjectedColumnsFor(objects.get(object))` is called once per object and cached. It runs on the authored definition, the input the spec's `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` expects, and it handles both pre-injection and post-injection shapes. The predicate is not copied. The message is `unprovisionedAnchorVerdict` plus a consequence for the position, and the hint is `unprovisionedAnchorFix`. That matches the sibling shape (`validate-searchable-fields.ts`, `validate-sortable-fields.ts`).
3. **`RULE_EXPLANATIONS`** gains the `ai-context-field-unprovisioned` key, and the `ai-context-field-unknown` paragraphs are rewritten. **Accurate and consistent with each other.**
   - "`owner_id` under `ownership: 'org'`" and "any of them under `systemFields: false`" match the `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` table: the `ownership: 'org' | 'none'` row gets no ownership anchors, and `systemFields: false` gets nothing.
   - The unknown entry hands the external case to the new id, and the new entry hands an undefined name back to the unknown id.
   - The new entry reuses `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_CAUSE` and `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_REMEDY`. Its costs for each position ("empty on every record", "no body", "no rows", "arbitrary order") match the `noRows` and `orderBy` message clauses word for word.
   - The new id joins both `UNPROVISIONED_ANCHOR_*` doc lists.
4. **Metadata accept set: unchanged.** No `packages/spec/**` path is touched and nothing new becomes authorable, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
5. **Test-only change:** `service-record-context` folds `injected-system-columns.test.ts` into `record-context-tools.test.ts`. Nothing publishes.
   - All three original cases are kept and their assertions are byte-identical. The only differences are the rename `CALL` → `BRIEF_CALL`, `sys_user` hoisted to `SYS_USER`, and the helpers scoped inside the describe.
   - The deleted file has no remaining reference anywhere in the tree. The lint test's cross-reference comment now points at the shared harness.
   - The scope-note pin (7182743879) is real. The registered `task` carries `owner_id`, `created_by` and `updated_by`, each pointing at `sys_user`. Named `owner_id` reads `[t1]` and named `created_by` reads `[t2]`: two distinct rows, which proves the named link is the one used. Omitted, the list is left out silently. A door serving declared fields only resolves no link.
6. **Removed or renamed: none.** No export, rule id or explain key is removed or renamed.

Findings:

- **N1 (nit):** the `where`, `orderBy`, link and `fields` consequence clauses ("no rows", "an arbitrary order", "empty on every record") were not measured for `get_record_context` over a remote table. They repeat the measured readings of `page-field-unprovisioned` and `sort-field-unprovisioned`. The PR body declares this, and the executor maps an absent value to `null`, which agrees with "empty". Accepted as declared, no change owed.
- **N2 (nit, inherited, not introduced here):** an `external` object whose `external.columnMap` maps a remote column onto an injected name, without declaring that field, is still warned. The cause is that the spec's `unprovisionedInjectedColumns` does not read `columnMap`; only `isOwnerAnchorUnprovable` adds that check. Every sibling `*-field-unprovisioned` rule shares this, the rule's own hint resolves it (declare the column), and the finding is a warning. If anyone owns it, it is a spec-predicate follow-up, not this card.
- **N3 (nit):** `skills/objectstack-ai/references/context-packs.md` (the rule table, lines 108-113) does not list `ai-context-field-unprovisioned`. `skills/**` is fenced off this card and no gate reads the table. The carrier is the area seat, which should file it as a follow-up card per `filing-gate.md` rather than leave it "noted, not filed".

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/37432-ai-context-field-unprovisioned.md` moves `@objectstack/lint` at `patch` and names only that package. It carries both declaration lines at line start: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The PR body carries the same pair.
- **The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration is right.** The diff widens the public surface by one exported constant and one emitted advisory rule id, and narrows nothing.
- **`patch` is right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: with `Metadata-protocol: none`, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level agrees with the seat's precedent on #37418 / PR #37438.
- `service-record-context` changes only a test file, so it rightly has no changeset entry.
- The card body's `Clause-②: no` is superseded by amendment 7203965629. The two carriers the readers use, the PR body and the changeset, both read `yes (widening)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** none, so there is nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviation 1** (judged sites widened to `where`, `orderBy` and the link): accepted. The card's own words cover it ("every place the rule reads a field map"), and amendment 7203965629 records it.
- **Dev deviations 2 to 5** (CI polling, background builds, worker-capped vitest, PR-body footer): process only, with no contract effect. Accepted.
- **Out-of-scope finding** (skills table): see N3, escalated to the area seat as the carrier.
- **`security_findings: none`:** concur. No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour.
- **Claim line:** the claim 7202779669 still reads `Clause-②: no` at line start. The correction lives in amendment 7203965629, and the PR body, which is the owed-face reader's carrier, reads `yes (widening)`. Consistent, and nothing owed.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):** no finding. `validate-ai-context.ts` is an author-time check over metadata. It runs no query, materialises no ids and does no in-app join. The fold adds only test code.
- **CI:**
  - On the head's latest attempts: 59 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure.
  - `Test UI (2/16)` failed on its first attempt (job 140183953126) at `ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.sharedWidgets-10179.test.tsx:194`: a label "Due" with no associated form control. On the rerun the shard (job 140194533944) and the `Test UI` aggregate (job 140198585086) went green; the superseded aggregate was 140190289726.
  - The diff cannot reach that test. `FormPage.tsx` imports only `@object-ui/*`, `@objectstack/spec/api`, `@objectstack/spec/ui` and `./submitRedirect`, which imports only `@objectstack/spec/ui`.
  - The diff changes `@objectstack/lint`, which the console reaches only through app-shell's lazy `capabilityLint.ts` import, and a `service-record-context` test file. Neither is in that test's import graph, and `packages/spec` is untouched.
- **PR author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so there is no further login to name.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37432-ai-context-unprovisioned`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**
